title: The Literal First Bug
hook: Your smartphone's glitches are named after a dead insect from 1947.
script: Your smartphone's glitches are named after a dead insect from 1947. In the late forties, engineers worked on the Mark II computer. This machine was a monolith of three thousand vacuum tubes and five thousand relays. Why did a room-sized calculator suddenly stop working? Technician William Morton found a real moth trapped in Relay 70, Panel F. The insect was the size of a matchbox, but it caused a total electrical short. He taped the moth into the logbook as the first actual case of bug being found. Every single line of modern code now traces its name back to that one moth. The original insect is still preserved today at the Smithsonian. Do you think we'd call them bugs if the insect was never found?
